text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Attack on Moslems in Mostar, bombs on Catholic churches and special ties between the Serbs from both sides of the Drina river smack of fresh division of Bosnia, the daily says in a commentary.

- Following recent attacks on Catholic churches, Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) calls for the international community to pay more attention on Sarajevo since it is the key to Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation and overall relations in Bosnia.
- "Whoever is throwing bombs is an enemy of Bosnia," spokesman for the ruling Moslem Party of Democratic Action (SDA) Ismet Grbo says after the bomb attack on a Catholic church in Sarajevo.

- Perpetrators of the February 10 incident in Mostar, when one Moslem was killed and 22 were wounded, have not been arrested yet, chief of the High Representative's Office in Mostar Sir Martin Garrod says.

- European Parliament proposes halting financial aid for Croat-controlled west Mostar until the Moslems are guaranteed the right to return, the daily quotes a yet unpublished document issued by the European Parliament.

- An international police's report on the February 10 incident in Mostar will be expanded and the final version will be revealed next week, chief of the International High Representative's office in Mostar, Sir Martin Garrod says.
- Senior Bosnian Moslem-Croat federation officials agree that financial and judicial institutions in cantons must be established promptly in order to expedite tax collection.

- The International Criminal Tribunal for former Yugoslavia in Hague issues a stern warning to Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation Defence Minister Ante Jelavic to open Bosnian Croat war archives to the tribunal by Thursday.

- The last attack on the Saint Joseph's Catholic church in Sarajevo can be interpreted as a special war against Bosnia and shows inability of the local police to prevent it, the daily says in a commentary.
- 361 criminal acts have been committed in Bosnia's Moslem- Croat federation within the last year in which 116 persons were killed, federal interior ministry says.

- Representatives of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) informed Bosnian co-prime minister Haris Silajdzic that the agency has invested $58 million in 1996 and will invest another $52 million during this year for various projects in Bosnia.

- Health workers in Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation will go on strike on Thursday over unpaid salaries in 1996 and other social problems. It is unclear whether their colleagues from the Croat part of the federation will dfollow suit.

- Since the publishing of lists of candidates for upcoming elections in Croatia, threats to Moslem candidates to leave the country have increased, Moslem Party of Democratic Action's candidate in the Croatian town of Rijeka Ibrahim Ruznic says. --Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
